newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA STOCKS CLOSE LOWER ON RETAIL SALES.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA STOCKS CLOSE LOWER ON RETAIL SALES.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Wednesday after retail investors sold highly capitalised blue chips, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 3.5 points down at 850.7. Blue chips Hatton National Bank fell 10.25 rupees to 289.75, Development Finance five to 315, John Keells Holdings 2.25 to 370.
"Retailers drove the market as institutional investors, both local and foreign, were largely on the sidelines," said Gordon Nadesan of brokerage CT Smith.
Turnover was 66.9 million rupees. Foreign buying totalled 8.6 million rupees and selling was worth 14 million.
"The NDB (National Development Bank) share offers have kept local and foreign institutional investors busy," said Sanjeeva Guneardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
NDB last week made a foreign offer of 16.5 million shares at 260 rupees each and said on Wednesday that it was making a local offer of 900,000 shares at 250 rupees, on August 28.
The shares comprise part of the convertible debentures which were held by the government.
Brokers say the all-share should be range-bound until there is some fresh news to move it. --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
